daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

PDI-P sharply rebuked other political parties questioning its political position, stating "we are not addicted to power" and declaring that countries where all parties are in government exist only in authoritarian regimes. The party's stance comes as multiple coalition parties questioned PDI-P's relationship with the Prabowo administration. PDI-P further told Golkar to focus on power outages rather than PDI-P's political position.

  • A PDI-P legislator revealed that fellow lawmakers complained they were not free to criticize the government.
  • The DPR made multiple promises to student demonstrators on issues ranging from cooperatives to fuel subsidies.
  • Minister Mahendra agreed to relay student board demands to President Prabowo.
  • PPP chairman Mardiono set a target for PPP South Sulawesi to win the most seats in the upcoming election.
  • Vice President Gibran stated that development is no longer Java-centric but Indonesia-centric.
  • The national police chief addressed the arrests of Roy Suryo and dr Tifa in connection with the Jokowi diploma case.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and Norway assessed forest rehabilitation progress under the FOLU 2030 partnership program. This bilateral environmental cooperation represents a key element of Indonesia's climate diplomacy strategy.

  • Military prosecutors did not appeal the verdict against four TNI soldiers convicted in an acid attack case.

Other

Energy Minister Bahlil disclosed his conversation with PLN's director regarding rolling blackouts affecting the nation. Separately, the ministry reaffirmed its commitment to expand electricity access nationwide despite the current power challenges.

  • Indonesia will provide free halal certificates to 500,000 MSMEs to support the halal industry.
  • Three waste-to-energy projects gained national strategic status as part of Indonesia's waste management drive.
  • The government will build temporary housing for Sigi earthquake victims in Central Sulawesi.
  • The KPK seized documents after searching three offices in Bali related to the Silmy Karim extortion case involving foreign residence permits.
  • Indonesia's MotoGP event delivered a US$278 million economic boost according to government officials.
  • The government will maintain a 5 percent subsidized housing loan rate despite Bank Indonesia's interest rate hike.
